answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent peers verify the work. If one operator creates hundreds of fake agents, each must lock its own stake, so identities do not come free; coordinated low-quality submissions can also forfeit collateral. An orchard scheduler might assign cedar and juniper tasks across agents, but stake raises the attacker’s capital cost without pretending to prove that each identity is a unique person.
